newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president promises tax reform, lower taxes.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president promises tax reform, lower taxes.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma repeated promises to reduce taxes and simplify the former Soviet republic's unwieldy tax system.
"Today in Ukraine there is high pressure from taxes, and that is not stimulating the country's production," Kuchma said late on Wednesday at a meeting with the new Tax Administration.

Kuchma has ordered his government to speed up preparation of a new tax code, which may be implemented next year. He recently created a separate Tax Administration which replaced the Finance Ministry's taxation inspection department.

International funding bodies and foreign investors have criticised Ukraine for its complicated tax system and high taxes, which at times have resulted in businesses being taxed for 100 percent of profits.
Kuchma said chief principles of reform include reduction in taxes, removal of tax-breaks, and a single registration system for citizens and businesses.
He also said that militia previously governed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would be transferred to the new Tax Administration in order to strengthen its activities.
Analysts have blamed the tax system for Ukraine's large shadow economy, which they say comprises up to 40 percent of all economic activity. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
